customManagers.description: Version pins no built-in manager reads, under pkgs/ and hosts/: from-source and release-binary packages, container tags, PyPI overrides. Opt-in per pin via a `# renovate:` comment directly above a `version`-like binding (`version`, `brainVersion`…), so the ones left out stay out; each excluded pin says why in its own file.
Commit pins on untagged upstreams: Renovate follows the branch head (git-refs) and rewrites `rev`. No versioningTemplate: git-refs needs its default `git` versioning.
The Renovate version the self-hosted workflow runs (.github/workflows/renovate.yml), so Renovate keeps itself current.

lockFileMaintenance.description: All day Monday, not the default 'before 4am': GitHub drops most of the 2-hourly scheduled runs, and none landed in 00:00–04:00 UTC on a Monday from 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-19, so no lock-file PR was opened for four weeks.

packageRules.description: gramps-web-nix is pinned on purpose: a3f86d5 (gramps-web-api 3.17.0) fails pythonRuntimeDepsCheck against our nixpkgs — needs gramps>=6.0.4, pillow<12, sifts>=1.1 plus yclade/authlib/gramps-gedcom7/flask-smorest. See the comment on the input in flake.nix. Renovate proposed it as #438, it was merged, and it broke main. Re-enable once gramps-web-nix carries those deps.

hermes-agent is pinned to a release tag in flake.nix and follows nixpkgs-unstable. Only plain vX.Y.Z tags: upstream also cuts daily `vX.Y.Z+canary.<date>` snapshots of main, and its old date tags (v2026.9.24) sort above v0.x as semver. A bump whose nix/lib.nix names a nodejs_* our nixpkgs-unstable lacks fails `eval rpi5` on the PR. A green PR can still drop something the config names, so read the release notes before approving.
prBodyNotes: Read the release notes before approving. Checks catch eval and build breaks, not a bundled plugin that moved: v0.22 moved the `holographic` memory provider (`memory.provider` in hosts/rpi5/agents/hermes/hermes.nix) to the plugin catalog, and Hermes would have started without its fact store.

packageRules.description: claude-code follows the `next` dist-tag, not `latest`. The two diverge by days and the gap is load-bearing: Anthropic gates models on the client version, so `latest` (2.1.278 when this was written) answers --model claude-opus-5-5 with a 400 telling you to upgrade, while `next` (2.1.280) serves it and resolves the bare `opus` alias to it. Following `latest` would mean the newest model is unreachable for as long as the tags disagree. The cost is riding a pre-release channel on purpose — read the release notes on the PR.
t3code follows nightly pre-releases on purpose: the Mac runs the T3 Code (Nightly) app, and a stable rpi5 server behind it loses access to its sessions over T3 Connect.
Keep each agent CLI's Nix flake source tag and mirrored package version in one update PR.

pkgs/ and hosts/ bumps: Renovate rewrites `version` via the regex manager, and postUpgradeTasks recomputes the fixed-output hashes beside it (scripts/nix-fix-hashes.py) before committing, so the bump and its hashes land as one commit. Needs the self-hosted runner (.github/workflows/renovate.yml) — the Mend app ignores postUpgradeTasks. Dependency-store hashes (pnpmDeps, vendorHash, cargoHash) are recomputed by building that one fixed-output derivation; the `hashes` check stays as the gate for anything the script still cannot speak for. The `src` half only holds because every fetcher under pkgs/ passes an explicit version-bearing `name` — see pkgs/README.md, 'Fixed-output names'.
prBodyNotes: Pinned hashes (`hash`, per-platform hashes, `imageDigest`, `npmDepsHash`, `pnpmDeps.hash`, `vendorHash`, `cargoHash`) were recomputed in this same commit by `scripts/nix-fix-hashes.py` (postUpgradeTasks, self-hosted Renovate in .github/workflows/renovate.yml).
A package the script cannot `callPackage` with `{ }` (e.g. one fed by a flake input) is reported, not fixed — check the `hashes` log, and fix it with `lib.fakeHash` + a real build.
Check the upstream changelog before merging — a major bump may also need module changes. `affine-mcp-server` 1.x → 3.x, for instance, reworks authentication.
